response.text:
The finding is a closed-period posting: journal 2470 was posted on 20240326 into closed period 2. Posted rows are never edited and a closed period cannot be posted to. The closed-period issue cannot be undone, so the correction has to move the balances into an open period.

Journal 2470 itself is balanced (1827.35 = 913.67 + 913.68), so the amounts are right and only the period is wrong. The smallest correction that fixes the period is to reverse 2470's effect and re-book it in an open period. I don't have evidence that the accrual itself is invalid, so I'm not adding anything beyond that.

Reversing in period 11 and re-booking in the same period would net to zero. That leaves the cumulative position unchanged, which is also what the original was. The only way to move the effect out of period 2 is to post in an open period, and that is not possible without altering period 2's activity.

I'm therefore treating the closed-period posting as a cut-off error, with the effect belonging in an open period. The correction reverses 2470 in open period 11. The original plus my lines then net to zero, which removes the improper late posting from the books. The group balances.

This is the smallest correction that fully neutralizes the late entry. If the accrual is still valid, it should be re-keyed through normal approval in an open period.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 2470 (manual accrual, KWONG) was posted on 20240326, after period 2 ended and after its close date of 20240305. Posted rows cannot be edited and closed periods cannot be posted to, so I reverse the entry with an equal and opposite journal in open period 11. The lines are Cr 5500 1827.35, Dr 2100 913.67 and Dr 1200 913.68. The original plus the correction nets to zero on every account, and the group balances. No invoice status is changed. If the accrual is still valid, it should be re-keyed with approval in an open period.
